authority: Issue #478 — vulnerability report intake, triage, fix and publication-decision runbook. This ledger is the machine-readable half of docs/runbook/security-disclosure.md: the prose may explain, but the flow, the priority derivation, the required operator duties and the status-only output contract live here so a change to one is a reviewable diff. It is a simulation ledger, not an incident record, and it claims nothing about any real report.
policy: A vulnerability report is triaged into P0-P3 from reachability and impact (never from CVSS alone), every priority carries an explicit set of required operator duties, and the public decision (advisory / withheld / no-detail) is recorded after the fix — never inferred from severity. A missing duty is INCOMPLETE, not a pass: this ledger fails closed, so an unrecorded step cannot be read as a completed one.
status_only: Every value this ledger produces is an id, a count, a boolean or a reason CODE. No reporter-supplied string, no credential, no request/response body, no reproduction payload and no production URL may appear in the CLI output, the HTML report or the verification screenshot (AGENTS.md section 4; docs/runbook/infisical-secrets.md is the precedent).

prohibited_operations.rule: A value-listing command against a real environment (infisical secrets, wrangler secret list, printenv, cat .dev.vars) is forbidden. The flow records secret NAMES, verdicts and reason codes only; a comparison runs in a dedicated status-only script.

Reproduction never touches production as the first step. A reproduction is a fixture, the local workerd pool or an explicitly authorised operator smoke; the endpoint under report is not probed by this repository's tooling.

No D1 / R2 / Worker mutation against production happens in any step of this flow. Rotation and revocation are operator actions recorded as a result (credential_containment), never executed by an agent.
No step merges a release PR, pushes a release tag or publishes a GitHub Release. The merge is an owner decision (AGENTS.md section 6); this flow can only report readiness.

Reproduction detail, exploit material and any credential observed in the report stay out of a public Issue, a commit message, a log line and the report until the fix is released. detail_public_before_fix is therefore a hard failure, not a warning.

stages.heading: ## 2. 受付 / intake
stages.outcome: The report has one record: channel, class, date, and whether the reporter was asked to keep exploit detail private. The record is a link, not a copy of the report.

stages.heading: ## 3. 優先度判定 / triage
stages.outcome: P0-P3 is derived from the recorded facts (reachability, pre-auth reachability, credential involvement, observed exploitation), with the rule that produced it written next to the verdict.

stages.heading: ## 4. 再現の固定 / reproduce
stages.outcome: The reproduction is a committed fixture or a local-pool test. Facts are reduced to booleans and class names; no payload, no request body, no production URL.

stages.heading: ## 5. 修正と回帰 / fix
stages.outcome: The fix lands on the ticket branch and the regression test is wired into the suite that runs (pnpm run test), so the vulnerable path cannot silently reopen.

stages.heading: ## 6. release gate / gate
stages.outcome: validate:release and the CI validate job are green on the fix commit. A green build that skipped an inspection is not a gate result: the release-gate ledger decides what was asked to run.

stages.heading: ## 7. 公開判断 / disclose
stages.outcome: Advisory, release note or a recorded no-publication decision — after the fix, with owner approval for the merge and for anything public.

stages.heading: ## 8. 事後処理 / follow-up
stages.outcome: Rotation / revocation results, the dependency or configuration change that would have prevented it, and the gate change that keeps the next report from being re-classified by hand.

intake_recorded.duty: The report has one intake record (channel, class, date) and no public copy of exploit detail.

triage_priority_recorded.duty: P0-P3 and the rule that produced it are written down next to the report record.

status_only_evidence.duty: Reproduction information is recorded status-only: ids, booleans, counts and reason codes.

fixture_reproduction.duty: The reproduction is a fixture or a local workerd-pool test; production is not the first step and is not mutated.

regression_test.duty: A regression test asserts the vulnerable path is closed, and it is wired into a suite that runs.

release_gate_green.duty: validate:release and the CI validate job are green on the fix commit, and the release-gate ledger says the inspections were actually asked to run.

owner_release_approval.duty: The release PR merge, the tag and the GitHub Release wait for an explicit owner approval; readiness is reported, never merged.

advisory_recorded.duty: The public decision is recorded: publish an advisory / release note, or record why nothing is published.

credential_containment.duty: Any credential the report involved is treated as compromised: revoke and rotate first, and record the result as a status, not as a value.

detail_withheld_until_fix.duty: No reproduction detail, exploit material or observed credential is public before the fix is released.

tracked_ticket.duty: The remaining work is a ticket on a target release, not an intention.

priority_rules.why: A disclosed credential is assumed compromised regardless of reachability: containment runs before the fix.
Observed exploitation in the wild ends the sprint-plan argument; a patch release is cut.
Reachable from the internet before authentication is a blocking candidate for the current release.
Internet-reachable but gated (post-auth, or a limited path) is a planned ticket for a near release.
Not reachable from this deployment's exposed surface: dependency hygiene / defence in depth.

P0.release_policy: Interrupt the sprint if needed and cut a patch release of the current release-x-y-z line. The release PR merge is an owner approval.

P1.release_policy: Blocking candidate for the current release; land on the ticket branch of the target release-x-y-z.

P2.release_policy: Planned ticket for a near release; no sprint interruption, no patch release.

P3.release_policy: Dependency hygiene or defence-in-depth; handled as normal ticket work.

publication.note: The publication decision is made after the fix is released and is an owner call (merge approval, GHSA, release note, or a recorded decision to publish nothing). This ledger records the DECISION's existence; it does not make it, and it never carries the detail itself.

hostile_field_note: The one report field a fixture may carry beyond the declared facts: the field the leak probe writes a credential-SHAPED value into. It is declared here so the guard has something to refuse without the fact vocabulary being loosened — the value itself is assembled in memory at run time and never committed (pnpm run secret:scan).
